messages:
Alice (Product): Quick sync notes — we need to lock decisions for customer-managed networking in private deploys (VPC/on-prem). Main asks: zero-downtime upgrades, IP-preservation for migrations, and clear packaging flags for offline installs. Who picks what?
Ben (Eng-Net): Customers keep asking for BGP peering + preserved IPs. Biggest technical hitch is operator rolling upgrade while keeping tenant IP mappings stable.
Carla (Solutions): FYI ACME raised that they cannot accept any IP renumbering — route flip only. Means we need an announcement strategy.
Dave (Field): Also ran into conntrack drops after kernel patches — customers see 5-10m outage unless we drain properly. Need a playbook.
Ben (Eng-Net): Proposed approach: perform graceful route handoff via VRFs and staged BGP announcements, keep old route active until traffic is drained. NAT fallback if peering fails.
Alice (Product): Good. What's the rollout complexity (operator + installer changes)?
Ben (Eng-Net): Rough plan: operator implements graceful drain + BGP CRUD, installer exposes `--preserve-ips` and `--canary` flags. We'll orchestrate announcements in canary waves.
Carla (Solutions): Customers asked for explicit rollback token and audit trail. Suggested CLI example: 
```bash
./install.sh --preserve-ips --canary=10 --rollback-token=<token>
```
Ben (Eng-Net): We'll persist rollback-token in the operator CR and emit events to the audit log. Also need a k8s finalizer to ensure cleanup.
Dave (Field): Runbook must include: preflight IP-sanity check, circuit owner signoff, 12h staging canary, post-canary validation steps. Add a checklist for emergency rollback.
Alice (Product): Draft launch criteria: (1) successful canary on >=2 staging customers, (2) runbook + customer comms published, (3) rollback automation tested end-to-end.
Carla (Solutions): Add SLO targets: peering handshake <15s, request error rate <5% during canary. Also require metrics exported for route-flap and neighbor state.
Ben (Eng-Net): Risk: some customers have managed CPE that blocks BGP changes. We need NAT fallback and explicit cost/latency callouts in comms.
Alice (Product): Actions: Ben — prototype operator changes + NAT fallback next sprint. Carla — draft customer-facing runbook and comms. Dave — compile field preflight checklist + top 5 strict-net customers. I'll own the launch criteria doc.
deploy-bot: New task created: PROD-4179 'Preserve IPs for private deploys' assigned to @Ben (Eng-Net). :white_check_mark:
Ben (Eng-Net): Quick Q — do we require maintenance windows in the installer? I want explicit enforcement to avoid surprise upgrades.
Alice (Product): Yes — add `--maintenance-window` (RFC3339 tz) and require operator to respect it by default.
Carla (Solutions): Draft notes are here (internal draft): https://redwood.internal/notes/preserve-ips-vpc-onprem — please add examples.
Dave (Field): Tagging legal for compliance checklist — @legal can you review the rollback audit requirements?
Alice (Product): Thanks everyone. We’ll reconvene in 48h with updates on the action items. :handshake:
